newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ apple-loading system at Napier to be closed.
newsitem.headline: NZ apple-loading system at Napier to be closed.

text.p: The New Zealand Apple and Pear Board (ENZA) said on Tuesday the NZ$45 million Omniport automatic spiral apple-loading machine at the Port of Napier was to be closed and either sold internationally or scrapped.

In a joint statement Board chief executive Gary Smith and Omniport chairman Jim McLay said the two parties had reached an agreement which recognised the spiralveyor system could no longer be used because of ENZA's export market requirements.
Omniport agreed to build the spiralveyor to load individual apple cartons in 1988. ENZA was committed to use the facility for 11 seasons from its opening in 1990.
Smith said when ENZA entered the agreement it was confident that most apple exports would be in individual cartons (break bulk form) and committed to Omniport on that basis.
However, Smith said export markets now required the use of pallets.
McLay said the two parties had entered into a revised commercial relationship.
"Omniport will continue to provide conventional stevedoring services to ENZA for at least the next five years," he said.

McLay said satisfactory arrangements had been negotiated with bank Westpac, which financed the facility, and the Port of Napier and decommissioning of the spiralveyor would probably take about nine months.
He said the machine had been well maintained and could be useful to a port that handled break-bulk cargo such as cartons, bags and carcasses.
Omniport would look for buyers on a world-wide basis.
McLay said if the facility, which also included depalletisers and a conveyor system, could not be sold in that period it would be scrapped.
